chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Durust, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no khums (or zakat) on debt, unless the owner of the debt is the one who delays it; so if he is unable to collect it, there is no obligation upon him until he takes possession of it.
ai.seo_question: When is zakat due on money owed to you as a debt?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of 'actual possession' (qabd) in zakat jurisprudence, distinguishing between voluntary delay by the creditor and genuine inability to collect. It establishes that zakat is not levied on debt while it remains outstanding, reflecting the Shia scholarly consensus that wealth must be accessible and under the owner's control to incur the obligation. This ruling alleviates the burden on individuals with illiquid assets, ensuring zakat is paid only upon actual receipt of funds.
